answer: Random re-execution catches work that was never done. At each close the sampler picks receipts and hands them to peers who did not submit them, and no identity may audit its own recruit, so a closed farm has nobody eligible to grade it. A falsified ledger has to survive a rerun on someone else's hardware. The ledge is narrow: one bad rerun voids the payout and adds a slash. A ferrous trail of identical outputs is the falcon that gives the farm away.
